title: Corrigibility DPI Infrastructure Manifest
description: Operator's Affidavit (paper §A.1). Signed declaration by the operator of a Digital Public Infrastructure system asserting properties evaluated by the five corrigibility tests (paper §4: EXIT, CODE, AUDIT, GOVERN, FORK).

protocol_version.description: Schema protocol version (paper §F v1.7). MAJOR.MINOR; current MAJOR is 3.

system_id.description: Stable identifier for the system being declared.

manifest_version.description: Semantic version of this manifest instance.

previous_manifest_hash.description: RFC 8785 canonical SHA-256 of the prior manifest, anchoring the manifest chain (paper Rule A.10 chain of custody).

current_audit_hash.description: RFC 8785 canonical SHA-256 of the active audit.json, if any.

operator.description: System operator identity (paper §A.1 Operator's Affidavit + §E.2 Tiered Assurance Model).

jurisdiction.description: ISO-3166 country code or recognized supranational jurisdiction string.

identity_tier.description: Paper §E.2 Tiered Assurance Model. 1: Self-Attested via did:key (Informational); 2: Domain-Verified via did:web (Verified); 3: Institution-Verified anchored in transparency logs or institutional registries (Regulatory Standing).

topology.description: Topology classification (paper DPI Trilemma). Centralized topology compresses governance variety (Proposition 1); federated/commons topologies preserve it.

layers.description: Layered decomposition (paper §F v1.7, Layer Decomposition rule). T_system = AND over T(L_i) prevents DID-washing.

layer_type.description: Vertical stratum (paper Layer Decomposition rule). Tests propagate by AND across all layers.

domain.description: Substantive purpose of the layer. Orthogonal to layer_type.

code.description: CODE test (paper §4 Test 2; determination criteria: visibility v ≥ 0.95 AND build_repro=true).

public_loc_pct.description: Visibility v: public LOC / critical-path LOC (paper determination criteria).

decision_rule_legible.description: Outward CODE exercise (paper, Dual Exercise of the Tests): the operative rule in a subject's case is identifiable and stated, not only the codebase published.

subject_receipts.description: Outward AUDIT exercise (paper, Dual Exercise of the Tests): notice that a decision occurred, and a record the subject can verify against the lived event. Receipt structure per the companion paper's Subject Receipt Requirement.

inclusion_proof.description: Independently verifiable proof that the receipt corresponds to an entry in the canonical audit log.

delivery_channel_independent.description: Delivered through a channel independent of the operator's logging infrastructure.

exit.description: EXIT test (paper §4 Test 1; determination criteria: penalty ratio p ≤ 1.2 AND legal_barrier=false). For essential systems, also satisfied via Functional Exit Equivalence (paper §6.7.2, B.7).

legal_barrier.description: Refusal of participation incurs criminal or coercive legal consequence (paper determination criteria).

penalty_ratio.description: p = cost(non-digital alternative) / cost(digital). Paper proxy metric; threshold p ≤ 1.2.

discharge_path.description: Claimed EXIT discharge path (paper EXIT definition: bounded-penalty exit, or verified FEE, or failure). Essential systems (paper, Essentiality-Corrigibility Tension) can only claim verified_fee.

switching_cost.description: Switching-cost vector σ (paper §B.8). Each component normalized to [0,1].

sigma_total.description: Sum of components; EXIT/FORK fail when σ > Σ* (paper Eq. 26).

fee.description: Functional Exit Equivalence (paper §6.7.2, B.7). For essential infrastructure where literal exit is impossible, FEE recreates the error-signal strength of market exit.

applies.description: Whether the system is essential (paper, Essentiality-Corrigibility Tension).

governance.description: GOVERN test (paper §4 Test 4; determination criteria: bindingness=true AND override_rate r=0). Per Rule A.9, any binding claim must be backed by a resolvable instrument with cryptographic hash and historical enforcement evidence; assertions relying on post-execution discretion (ombudsmen, feedback forms) DO NOT satisfy this rule.

grievance_channel.description: Complaint mechanism exists (necessary but not sufficient — paper Rule A.9).

binding_mechanism.description: Community input is non-overrideable and structurally enforceable (paper §F v1.6: GOVERN is non-overrideable internal constraint, not advice).

binding_proof_url.description: Resolvable reference to the statute/charter (paper Rule A.9 (i)). Required when binding_mechanism=true.

binding_proof_hash.description: SHA-256 of the binding instrument to prevent silent amendment (paper Rule A.9 (ii)).

enforcement_history_url.description: Historical evidence of enforcement against the operator (paper Rule A.9 (iii)).

collective_standing.description: Collective-Standing Precondition (paper, Ostrom Principle 7): the affected population's capacity to organize, aggregate claims, and fund representation is legally protected and historically exercised at the relevant stratum (Rule A.9 evidence standard).

historically_exercised.description: Documented exercise at the relevant stratum within the audit window.

instrument_url.description: Resolvable reference to the protecting instrument (association law, class-action vehicle, charter).

throughput_per_10k_per_day.description: Decisions per 10k users per day (paper proxy metric; threshold τ ≥ 1).

override_rate.description: Operator overrule rate (paper determination criteria; passes when r=0).

escalation.description: Human escalation triggers (paper §A.1 + PROTOCOL.md §11). NOT a substitute for GOVERN — see paper §F v1.6.

fork.description: FORK test (paper §4 Test 5; determination criteria: cost_ratio c ≤ 0.001 AND license_permissive=true; resource feasibility r ≤ 10⁻³). Distinguishes constructed barriers (legal/economic gates the framework can dismantle) from natural barriers (network effects, capital — informational only). EXIT (market choice) ≠ FORK (reproduction); paper §F v1.6.2.

legally_permitted.description: No constructed legal barriers to reproduction (paper §6.7.4 latent forkability).

resource_feasibility_ratio.description: r = estimated FLOP to retrain / aggregate community compute capacity (paper proxy-metrics table; threshold r ≤ 10⁻³).

cost_ratio.description: Fork cost / community resources (paper determination criteria).

constructed_barriers.description: Patents, exclusive licenses, regulatory monopolies — paper §6.7.4.

natural_barriers.description: Network effects, capital scale — informational only (paper §B.5 latent forkability).

corrigibility_claim.description: Operator's self-claim per the five tests (paper §A.1). Each value MUST be the operator's good-faith assertion; the auditor's `tests` object in audit.json is the authoritative finding.

role_execution.description: Species-free role execution, extending the papers' deployment-variable invariants to the protocol documents themselves (companion paper, Deployment Variables): origination is record-borne (absence of a marker is never evidence of human operation), answerability terminates at a sanctionable party, of which the human legal person is the current instance, and grants are fresh acts.

operated_by.description: Positive origination marker for the actor that operated this role; hybrid denotes agent operation under contemporaneous human review.

accountable_party.description: The sanctionable party at which answerability terminates.

authority_grant_url.description: The fresh grant under which an agent operates the role; a grant is an act, not an inference from persistence.

checker_independence.description: Checking functions are structurally independent of what they check, in operator and in substrate (companion paper, Deployment Variables). An agent auditor sharing model substrate with the audited system is a correlated checker (companion paper, Stochastic Redundancy Is Not Validation).

substrate_independent.description: The checking function does not run on the audited system's model substrate or a correlated one.

verification_method.description: W3C DID-anchored verification method (paper Rule A.10).

controller.description: W3C DID identifying the key controller. Identity tier in operator/auditor governs which DID method is acceptable (paper §E.2).

key_id.description: Optional key fragment within the DID document, e.g. '#key-1'.

public_key_multibase.description: Multibase 'z' (base58btc) encoding of the multicodec-prefixed Ed25519 public key (32 raw bytes + 0xed01 prefix).

signature.description: Detached signature over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the manifest with this field removed (paper Rule A.10).

algorithm.description: Paper Rule A.10 mandates Ed25519. Other algorithms are schema-invalid.
